record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: What is the correct quantum-field-theoretic description of the sine-Gordon model with a non-integrable boundary, and can techniques from quantum integrability still be adapted to study how integrability breaks down in that setting?

evidence.quote: Finally, at the back of our minds throughout this work was the thought to look at the corresponding quantum field theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the sine-Gordon model in 1+1 dimensions, defined on the half-line $x \le 0$ by the bulk Lagrangian density
$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{bulk}} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_t \phi)^2 - \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x \phi)^2 + \frac{m^2}{\beta^2}\bigl(\cos(\beta\phi) - 1\bigr),$$
where $\phi(t,x)$ is a real scalar field, $m>0$ is a mass parameter, and $\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ is the coupling. At the boundary $x=0$, impose a boundary potential
$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{bdy}} = -V_{\text{bdy}}(\phi(t,0)),$$
where $V_{\text{bdy}}$ is chosen so that the resulting boundary condition does not preserve the infinite tower of higher-spin local conserved charges of the bulk theory (i.e., the boundary condition is non-integrable, lying outside the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov family $V_{\text{bdy}}(\phi) = M\cos\!\bigl(\tfrac{\beta}{2}(\phi-\phi_0)\bigr)$).

The problems are:

(a) Provide a precise quantum-field-theoretic description of this half-line sine-Gordon model with non-integrable boundary potential: specify the Hilbert space, the renormalized Hamiltonian, the spectrum of asymptotic particle states (solitons, antisolitons, breathers, and possible boundary bound states), and the appropriate notion of reflection amplitude when bulk-integrability-preserving boundary Yang–Baxter relations fail.

(b) Determine to what extent techniques developed for quantum integrability on the half-line — such as the boundary bootstrap, reflection matrices satisfying the boundary Yang–Baxter equation, the truncated conformal space approach, and form-factor perturbation theory — can be adapted to quantitatively describe the breakdown of integrability induced by such non-integrable boundary terms, including the computation of corrections to reflection amplitudes, decay widths of formerly stable boundary bound states, and the modification of finite-size spectra.
artifact.status_search_result: Existing literature treats integrable boundary conditions of the sine-Gordon model (Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov, boundary bootstrap, half-line reflection matrices) and develops form-factor perturbation theory for non-integrable bulk perturbations, plus an asymptotic Lagrangian framework for general non-integrable boundary QFT. However, no comprehensive QFT description of sine-Gordon with a generic non-integrable boundary, nor a complete adaptation of integrability techniques to quantify the breaking, has been established; the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Sine-Gordon quantum field theory on the half-line with quantum boundary degrees of freedom
status_evidence.snippet: The sine-Gordon model on the half-line with a dynamical boundary is considered at quantum level; classical integrable boundary conditions are preserved at quantum level.
status_evidence.claim: Quantum half-line sine-Gordon is understood for integrable boundary conditions, but generic non-integrable boundaries are not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Non-integrable aspects of the multi-frequency sine-Gordon model
status_evidence.snippet: Form factor perturbation theory studies non-integrable perturbations of sine-Gordon in the bulk.
status_evidence.claim: FFPT addresses bulk non-integrability; boundary case remains less developed.

status_evidence.title: Finite size effects in integrable quantum field theory: the sine-Gordon model with boundaries
status_evidence.snippet: Finite-size spectrum analysis assumes integrable boundary conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Finite-size methods are formulated only in the integrable boundary case.
